A 26-year-old man visits the clinic one week following a motor vehicle collision where his vehicle was
impacted on the driver's side. During the incident, his head struck the driver's side window, resulting in
a concussion without loss of consciousness. While recovering from his injuries, he reports ongoing
headaches. His physical and neurological examinations are normal. During the osteopathic structural
examination, the following findings are noted: - Right greater wing of sphenoid appears more lateral
from midline - Left greater wing of sphenoid appears more medial to midline - Right occiput feels
medial - Left occiput feels lateral - Cranial rhythmic impulse measures approximately 5 cycles per
minute What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Cranial compression (B) Vertical strain
(C) Flexion/extension dysfunction (D) Torsion strain (E) Inferior vertical strain (F) Temporal bone
dysfunction (G) Sphenobasilar synchondrosis dysfunction (H) Lateral strain (I) Sidebending/rotation (J)
Superior vertical strain
 A. Cranial compression

B. Sidebending/rotation
C. Flexion/extension dysfunction
D. Vertical strain
E. Superior vertical strain
F. Torsion strain
G. Lateral strain
H. Temporal bone dysfunction
I. Inferior vertical strain
J. Sphenobasilar synchondrosis dysfunction
